title: Rumi on Joy: Dancing Like Specks in the Sunlight
subtitle: Eight Persian Sufi poems with English translation
yt_title: Rumi on Joy | 8 Persian Sufi Poems with English Translation
intro: Rumi is often remembered for longing and tears. But he was also a poet of overflowing joy.
He danced, he sang, and he wrote of the whole world clapping and turning.
Here are eight passages of joy from his Divan-e Shams.

poems.name: I Am Drunk

lines.fa: بستان قدح از دستم ای مست که من مستم
lines.en: Take the cup from my hand, drunken friend, for I am drunk;

lines.fa: کز حلقه هشیاران این ساعت وارستم
lines.en: this very hour I have escaped from the circle of the sober.

tafsir: In Sufi poetry, being drunk means being overwhelmed by divine love.
The sober are those who measure, worry and calculate.
Rumi says he has slipped out of their circle.
Joy, for him, begins where anxious calculation ends.

poems.name: No Stone in My Hand

lines.fa: در کف ندارم سنگ من با کس ندارم جنگ من
lines.en: I hold no stone in my hand; I have no quarrel with anyone.

lines.fa: با کس نگیرم تنگ من زیرا خوشم چون گلستان
lines.en: I am hard on no one, for I am happy, like a rose garden.

tafsir: This may be the simplest description of a joyful person ever written.
No stone in the hand. No fight with anyone.
Rumi says happiness makes us gentle.
A rose garden does not attack anyone. It just blooms.

poems.name: This Beating

lines.fa: ای دل ز کجا رسید این دم
lines.en: O heart, where did this breath come from?

lines.fa: ای دل ز کجاست این طپیدن
lines.en: O heart, where does this beating come from?

tafsir: Joy often arrives without explanation.
Suddenly the heart is beating faster, and we do not know why.
Rumi asks with wonder: where did this come from?
Sometimes the best answer to joy is just to ask the question, and enjoy it.

poems.name: The Whole World Dancing

lines.fa: دست زنان عقل کل رقص کنان جزو و کل
lines.en: Universal Reason is clapping; the part and the whole are dancing;

lines.fa: سجده کنان سرو و گل بر طرف سبزه زار
lines.en: cypress and rose bow down at the edge of the meadow.

tafsir: In this picture, everything joins the celebration.
Even Reason, which is usually serious, is clapping.
The trees and flowers bow like worshippers.
Rumi sees the world as one great gathering of praise.

poems.name: Specks in the Sunlight

lines.fa: در بزم بی‌هشی همه جان‌ها مجردند
lines.en: At the feast of selflessness all souls are free of everything,

lines.fa: رقصان چو ذره‌ها خورشان نور و روشنی
lines.en: dancing like specks of dust, their food light and brightness.

tafsir: Have you ever seen dust dancing in a beam of sunlight?
Rumi loved that image.
Souls that forget themselves are like those specks: light, turning, fed by the sun.
Joy is what happens when we stop being heavy with ourselves.

poems.name: A Laughing Paradise

lines.en: The whole world became a laughing paradise,
because of that walking cypress with a narcissus face.

tafsir: The walking cypress is the Beloved, tall and graceful.
One presence, and the whole world turns into paradise.
That is how love changes everything we look at.
Nothing outside has changed. Only the eyes have.

poems.name: I Found Sugar

lines.fa: گر ببینی طوطی جان مرا گرد لبش
lines.en: If you see the parrot of my soul around his lips,

lines.fa: می‌پرد پرک‌زنان که شکری را یافتم
lines.en: it flies about, fluttering: I have found sugar!

tafsir: In Persian poetry, parrots love sugar.
Here the soul is a parrot that has found the sweetest thing of all.
It cannot keep still. It flutters and announces it to everyone.
Real joy is like that. It wants to be shared.

poems.name: All Night

lines.fa: کو همه لطف که در روی تو دیدم همه شب
lines.en: Where is all the grace I saw in your face all night,

lines.fa: وآن حدیث چو شکر کز تو شنیدم همه شب
lines.en: and the sugar-sweet words I heard from you all night?

lines.fa: گرچه از شمع تو می‌سوخت چو پروانه دلم
lines.en: Though my heart was burning like a moth at your candle,

lines.fa: گرد شمع رخ خوب تو پریدم همه شب
lines.en: I flew around the candle of your lovely face all night.

tafsir: This is the memory of a night of joy with the Beloved.
Burning and delight are mixed together.
The moth burns, and still it cannot stop circling the light.
For Rumi, the deepest joy and the deepest love are the same fire.
